claims.claim: The incomplete globally k-image-bounded mortality upper bound is n^(k+1), and Kiefer/Ryzhikov ask whether it is tight.
For every fixed k>=2 and every n>=2k+2A_k*k!, the exact constants yield a binary strongly connected n-state example of threshold at least c_k*n^(k+1), hence Theta_k(n^(k+1)).
The maximum M_k(n) exists because there are finitely many letter relations and duplicates do not change shortest lengths.
The general subset bound is 2^n-1.
The quadratic order at k=1 is known.
Ryzhikov gives a binary deterministic cyclic queue and physical delay path; this queue action is known up to indexing.
Ryzhikov recalls the sharp arbitrary-alphabet deterministic mortality bound n(n+1)/2, attributed there to Rystsov.
The unrestricted NFA exponential lower bounds in Ryzhikov do not impose the global endpoint promise.
Ananichev Section 2 Lemma 2.1 reproduces Vorel appended-tail lemma: under its hypotheses, h new states increase reset threshold by r*h.
The packet period is lcm(ell_i), realized using sum(ell_i) states; pairwise coprime lengths give order n^k at fixed k.
Repeated failures, replacements, and resets cannot bypass the linear number of full delay events; global endpoint support stays bounded.
The b-action restricts to a permutation on P minus p_0, including the m=2 case.
The construction is strongly connected, globally k-image-bounded with least bound exactly k, and incomplete with threshold in [1+(m+1)L,1+(m+1)L+m^2].
Every singleton image is empty, singleton, or packet; this family is closed under a,b for every word.
Every queue/clock state can reach p_0 and p_0 can reach every state.
At b-boundaries the image uniquely equals T union E_eta; Q.b=P union S and first potential is m+1.
The disjoint injective queue action gives V(new)=|T|+epsilon and drop eta-epsilon for all intervals a^t b.
A drop occurs exactly on a present packet with all clocks terminal; L divides t+1 and interval costs >=L, including replacement events.
Deleting initial/trailing a-runs leaves a mortal word; exactly m+1 disjoint unit drops prove the lower bound.
Repeated a^(L-1)b decreases potential, preliminary forks cost <=m and occur <=m times; the procedure kills globally within the upper bound.
The parameter formulas produce m>=M>=n/(2A), M>=2, exact state count n, pairwise coprime ell_i, and L>=k!*M^k for every n>=N_k.
The Section 4 construction reaches lower bound k!/(2A_k)^(k+1)*n^(k+1), retaining binary and strong connectivity.
Shortest killing continuations have <=D nonempty subset visits and length <=D; killing n original rows sequentially gives <=nD.
Padding the increasing subset list by its maximum injects nonempty size<=k subsets into Q^k, so D<=n^k.
There are k b^2 paths and k^r b^(2r) paths from p_0 to itself; the endpoints merge.
The original source uses incomplete to mean existence of a mortal word rather than merely a missing transition.
